To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fractional differential equation can be used to describe the transient heat diffusion in a semiinfinite medium.

(1) The fractional-diffusion solution of the transient heat transfer equation is a very simple relation that relates the local value of timevarying temperature (or flux) to the corresponding transient heat (or flux).

the Laplace transform of the heat conduction equation can be transformed, using properties of the Laplacian operator, into a fractional differential equation, and that this transformation leads to a simple analytical solution that determines the local time variation of temperature (or heat ﬂux) along the boundary of a semi-inﬁnite domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a numerical model of the heat and mass transfer process in the drying of a thin layer of a porous material.
the development and validation of a new approach for the analysis of transient heat transfer in solids.
the development of a new approach for the solution of transient heat diffusion problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fractional heat diffusion equation is a very simple and powerful tool for solving transient heat transfer problems in semi-infinite domains.
, in spite of the simplicity of the solution, the fractional-diffusion model provides a good approximation of transient heat transfer in a semiinfinite body.
the use of the fractional-diffusion equation is not a panacea for the solution of transient heat transfer problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel method to solve transient heat conduction problems, which is based on fractional differential equations and the Laplace transform.
we have developed a simple analytical method for solving transient heat transfer problems.
we have shown that the Laplace transform of the transient heat diffusion equations leads to fractional differential equations, which can be solved analytically.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the heat transfer is unidirectional, the solution of the diffusion equation can be reduced to a single ordinary differential equation, which can be easily solved.
the fractional-diffusion equation is a very powerful tool for the analysis of transient heat transfer problems.
, for the transient case, the solution for local temperature (or heat transfer coefficient) can be determined without having to solve a partial differential equation.
